tweets.title: Conclusion: The dance SORTS the dance followers spatially into regions that correspond to directions in the world. Following a dance, you drift outwards, and ha
tweets.body: Conclusion: The dance SORTS the dance followers spatially into regions that correspond to directions in the world. Following a dance, you drift outwards, and hanging around there, you are more likely to sample another dance indicating the same direction --> a simple echo chamber!

tweets.title: Does this drift determine which dances they follow? YES! We can see a clear decision boundary! https://t.co/aWw3wkQaAS
tweets.body: Does this drift determine which dances they follow? YES! We can see a clear decision boundary! https://t.co/aWw3wkQaAS

tweets.title: How does this affect the dance followers? We find that they follow that drift as well! https://t.co/ykhuqWYLPF
tweets.body: How does this affect the dance followers? We find that they follow that drift as well! https://t.co/ykhuqWYLPF

tweets.title: Could the waggle angle predict where dancers dance? We measured how much dancers drift between consecutive waggle phases, and indeed: they drift a tiny amount i
tweets.body: Could the waggle angle predict where dancers dance? We measured how much dancers drift between consecutive waggle phases, and indeed: they drift a tiny amount into the direction of their waggle orientation! The longer the dance, the more pronounced the overall drift! https://t.co/2LQ1jBT8mR

tweets.title: Both food sites were at the same distance from the hive, hence the dances differed only in the waggle angles. Indeed we find that dances in different subregions
tweets.body: Both food sites were at the same distance from the hive, hence the dances differed only in the waggle angles. Indeed we find that dances in different subregions agree in their average angle. Look at that beautiful pattern! https://t.co/gZOD5lQMBJ

tweets.title: Do dancers start their dances already separated? We track the distance between dancers within and between the two groups and find: dancers separate gradually ov
tweets.body: Do dancers start their dances already separated? We track the distance between dancers within and between the two groups and find: dancers separate gradually over time! https://t.co/wBvGWhcdeY

tweets.title: We were curious: how do bees know where to dance, and can we see structure in the dance floor? We trained two groups of bees to opposite directions in the field
tweets.body: We were curious: how do bees know where to dance, and can we see structure in the dance floor? We trained two groups of bees to opposite directions in the field. Et voila: the two forager groups separate on the dance floor! https://t.co/oNevyyV6hx

tweets.title: They perform these dances on the “dance floor”, a small area close to the nest entrance. We used our automatic dance detection software to confirm this spatial
tweets.body: They perform these dances on the “dance floor”, a small area close to the nest entrance. We used our automatic dance detection software to confirm this spatial preference. https://t.co/v7Jtckm7N1

tweets.title: Honeybees perform “dances” to instruct their nestmates where to find food sources. They move forward waggling their body laterally ("waggle phase") and then cir
tweets.body: Honeybees perform “dances” to instruct their nestmates where to find food sources. They move forward waggling their body laterally ("waggle phase") and then circle back ("return phase") in left and right turns. The body angle encodes the direction of the food! https://t.co/nzTcLPCF23

tweets.body: Echo chambers in the honeybee dance communication! We automatically detected 100K waggle phases of dancing bees and found a fascinating aspect of how bees organize their colony space. A thread. https://t.co/UQdZRAxXH1
